title: SegPVSG: Panoptic Video Scene Graph Generation via Temporal Focusing and Generative Augmentation
claim: Relations in videos are temporally sparse and fragmented, and their category distribution is heavily long-tailed, making recognition difficult.
layout: 2 stacked panels: video frames with relation timeline above, bar chart below
description: The figure has two stacked panels separated by a dashed line. Panel (a), Temporal Sparsity, shows four video frames with colored borders (orange, green, blue, pink). Each frame has segmentation overlays labeled with entity IDs such as 18:adult, 19:adult, 10:ball and 4:grass. Colored triangle markers connect the frames to timeline bars below. The bars are for two entity pairs, adult_19 & grass_4 and adult_18 & ball_10. Colored relation labels sit on the bars: running on, walking on, standing on, holding, throwing. They occupy only short, scattered segments of long gray tracks. Panel (b) is a blue bar chart on a log scale of sample counts per relation predicate. A few head classes such as holding, on and standing on are very tall. A long tail of rare predicates is much shorter, with an ellipsis marking the gap. The eye goes first to the colorful frames, then to the steep drop in the bars.
caption: Critical challenges in PVSG. (a) Temporal Sparsity:
abstract: Panoptic Video Scene Graph Generation (PVSG) aims to identify relations between pixel-level entities in a video, serving as a novel paradigm for structured video parsing. However, this task faces two key challenges. First, the interactions between entities are temporally fragmented and sparse, meaning videos are dominated by irrelevant content with limited salient information. Second, the distribution of relations exhibits a significant long-tailed pattern, making models struggle to perform well on tail categories with insufficient data. To address these issues, we propose SegPVSG, an innovative, temporal-segment-aware PVSG framework consisting of two key components: TempFocusNet (TFN) and Relation-centric Generative Video Augmentation (RGVA) module. TFN is a localization-then-recognition network that improves PVSG performance by explicitly localizing and focusing on salient segments before relation recognition. Meanwhile, RGVA is a novel augmentation module that generates realistic, context-consistent video segments for rare relations and coherently inserts them into original videos. Our method outperforms prior methods by +3.53 mR@20 and +5.9 mR@50, demonstrating its effectiveness. The code is available at https://github.com/ticatt/SegPVSG.
